summary: Agoura Hills sits right at the western edge of the San Fernando Valley where the terrain buckles upward into the Santa Monica Mountains, and the city's southern boundary literally abuts the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area — meaning tens of thousands of acres of protected open space begin where the subdivisions end. That geography defines the daily texture: canyon-carved ridgelines frame the western sky at sunset, coyote sightings are routine, and trailheads connecting to a vast network of fire roads and singletrack are minutes from most front doors. The Ventura Freeway (US-101) bisects the city, which creates a real split — residential neighborhoods north and south of the highway feel like separate places connected mainly by a handful of overpasses, and pedestrian movement across that divide is limited. With a median household income near $172,000 and a median home value just above $1.07 million, the price-to-income ratio hovers around 6.2:1 — steep, though less extreme than coastal L.A. communities. This is overwhelmingly a bedroom community; the entertainment, tech, and healthcare jobs that support those incomes are mostly a 101 commute east toward Woodland Hills, Burbank, or Hollywood, and westward toward Thousand Oaks. Daily highs averaging 75°F with nearly ten hours of sunshine year-round make for a climate that barely requires a jacket, though summer afternoons in this inland valley push well past that average. The defining tradeoff is proximity to wildland against freeway dependence — the mountains are the reason to live here, and the 101 is the price of doing so.
